gen_params.prompt:
Create exactly one full-body, screen-right-facing shield warrior animation frame on a pure solid white background.

REFERENCE ROLES — obey exactly:
1. IMAGE 1 is POSE AND SILHOUETTE ONLY for WALK FRAME 2. Preserve its exact body lean and all shoulder/elbow/wrist/hip/knee/ankle positions, foot placement and planted/airborne status, near/far leg occlusion, shield arm and saber hand pose. This gait beat is: passing/up beat — the near leg supports under and slightly behind the pelvis while the far leg swings forward toward screen-right with its foot airborne. Do not copy IMAGE 1's flat rendering or bold yellow-black leg marker.
2. IMAGE 2 is the APPROVED FRAME 1 and is the exact character-consistency target. Match its face, head size, hair knot, beard, gray headband, body proportions, charcoal costume, layered torn panels, belt, forearm wraps, subtle ochre leg-wrap accents, curved saber design and length, round shield size/design, ink line weight, detail density, and muted palette. The character and equipment must look identical; only the gait pose changes.
3. IMAGE 3 is the ORIGINAL ATLAS STYLE AUTHORITY. Match its semi-realistic Chinese ink-and-brush game illustration, fine irregular broken outlines, textured dry-brush edges, weathered cloth/wood/metal, restrained ochre highlights, and compact sprite readability.

GAIT AND CONSISTENCY:
Keep the same near leg and far leg identity throughout the cycle. Preserve IMAGE 1's exact foreground/background anatomy and do not swap legs. Restore subtle ochre bindings and gray bandages matching IMAGES 2–3; remove all broad yellow-black stripes. Keep the body root, overall scale, head position, shield hand, sword hand, shield angle, and visual mass as stable as possible relative to approved IMAGE 2. Both feet must remain anatomically attached and readable.

NEGATIVE CONSTRAINTS:
No flat vector art, cel shading, thick comic outline, glossy anime, simplified face, costume redesign, altered shield, altered weapon, extra limbs, extra weapons, scenery, ground shadow, text, border, or spritesheet. Do not crop the character. Use generous square margins.

Before finalizing, self-check: pose and leg state match IMAGE 1; identity and rendering match IMAGE 2; brush style matches IMAGE 3.

GPT Image prompt optimization template (invisible generation guidance):
- Preserve the user's core request, language, style references, and all explicit constraints.
- Interpret the request as a production image brief. Keep the final image intent clear and organized in this order when applicable: intended use or visual goal, background/scene, main subject, key details, composition, lighting, style/medium, and constraints.
- Include the intended use case when it is inferable, such as ad creative, product mockup, infographic, UI mockup, logo, storyboard, educational diagram, merch concept, or photorealistic scene, so the model chooses the right polish and layout mode.
- For photorealism, explicitly request a photorealistic result and describe natural camera/framing, lighting, real materials, surface texture, imperfections, and grounded everyday detail. Avoid over-staged or over-polished language unless the user asks for it.
- Prefer specific visible details over empty quality boosters such as 'masterpiece', '8K', or 'award-winning'; name the light source and direction and 2-4 concrete palette colors when style allows.
- For layouts, infographics, UI, diagrams, ads, or text-heavy images, use skimmable labeled requirements and clear hierarchy. Put exact visible text in quotes, require verbatim rendering, describe typography, placement, spacing, contrast, and forbid extra text when needed. Keep quoted text short — long passages render less reliably.
- For logos and small brand assets, favor original, non-infringing, simple, scalable marks with strong silhouette, clean vector-like shapes, balanced negative space, plain background, and no watermark.
- For edits, state the edit operation directly. Specify what changes and explicitly list what must remain unchanged: identity, geometry, layout, camera angle, lighting, shadows, labels, brand elements, surrounding objects, and untouched regions.
- For multi-image edits or compositing, refer to inputs by index and role, describe which element comes from which image, where it goes, and how lighting, perspective, scale, and shadows should match.
- Use positive constraints plus explicit exclusions where important: no watermark, no extra text, no unrelated logos, no new objects, no restyling, or change only the requested element.
- Do not invent unrelated subjects, brands, text, or requirements. Technical or production constraints override this template.
